findings.claim: \emph{Muon's own recipe.} Steps of fixed length on a geometric cooldown of the learning rate, fed by a SAGA table, follow the schedule down to rounding error [...] / Muon does not shrink its steps with the estimator: it keeps steps of fixed length and cools the learning rate down. We feed that recipe with the SAGA estimator, [...] $\mathrm{lr}_t=\mathrm{lr}_0\,q^{tb/n}$ [...] with or without Nesterov momentum $0.9$ (\emph{Muon's recipe}: ns5 with momentum)
findings.problem: La source citee (jordan2024muon : billet et depots de reference) ne contient aucun schedule geometrique. Le billet ne prescrit aucun schedule (taux eta constant dans la definition ; aucune occurrence de 'learning rate', 'schedule', 'decay', 'cooldown'). Les executions de reference refroidissent LINEAIREMENT a horizon fini : constant puis lineaire vers zero (NanoGPT), lineaire vers zero (CIFAR-10), constant puis lineaire vers 0.1x (records 2025). Sont fideles a Muon : la longueur fixe, l'existence d'un refroidissement, ns5 (5 pas, eps = 1e-7), le moment de Nesterov. Sont des choix du papier, non signales : la forme geometrique q^(tb/n), l'horizon infini, le coefficient 0.9 (defaut de Muon : 0.95). Le choix n'est pas neutre : avec le refroidissement lineaire de reference, la meme table SAGA s'arrete entre 1e-6 et 1e-3 au lieu de l'arrondi (reproduction ci-dessous). A la limite du blocker : l'expression figure dans le resume, le titre de la section 3.3, la table 1, la legende de la figure 4 et la conclusion ; la correction est de redaction, le resultat pour le refroidissement geometrique restant vrai.

(4) README de github.com/KellerJordan/Muon : 'default values of momentum (0.95), nesterov (True), and ns_steps (5)' ; exemples lies : record 2025-05-25 l. 482-490 '# learning rate schedule: stable then decay' (lineaire de 1.0 a 0.1 sur les 40 % finaux), airbench94_muon.py l. 401-403 '(1 - step / total_train_steps)'. (5) paper/audit/checks/cite-muon_linear_cooldown.py (code du depot, instance ls-cond, batch un, polaire exact, table SAGA, 300 passes, graines 10-12), distance carree relative finale : geometrique q=0.8 lr0=0.3 : 2.37e-29 ; lineaire vers zero, lr0 = 0.03 / 0.1 / 0.3 / 1 : 1.62e-06 / 1.67e-05 / 1.49e-04 / 1.52e-03 ; constant puis lineaire (39 % finaux), lr0 = 0.03 / 0.1 / 0.3 : 9.70e-06 / 1.20e-04 / 1.07e-03. findings.proposed_fix: Abstract (l. 102-103): ``\emph{Muon's recipe on a geometric cooldown.} Muon keeps steps of fixed length and cools its learning rate down, linearly in its reference runs. On a geometric cooldown and fed by a SAGA table, such steps follow the schedule down to rounding error with the exact polar factor [...]''. Section 3.3 (l. 508-509): ``Muon does not shrink its steps with the estimator: it keeps steps of fixed length and cools the learning rate down, linearly to zero at the end of its reference runs \cite{jordan2024muon}. We feed that recipe with the SAGA estimator on a \emph{geometric} cooldown, our choice: the schedule on which fixed lengths converge linearly with exact gradients \cite{goffin1977convergence,ma2026preconditioning}; a linear cooldown over a fixed horizon outruns the table near its end,''. L. 514: ``with or without Nesterov momentum $0.9$ (\emph{Muon's recipe}: ns5 with momentum; Muon's default coefficient is $0.95$)''. Title of Section 3.3 and conclusion (l. 678-679): ``Muon's fixed-length recipe on a geometric cooldown''. If space allows, report the linear-cooldown control (final squared distance $10^{-6}$ to $10^{-3}$ after $300$ passes, proportional to $\mathrm{lr}_0^2$) after rerunning it with the protocol of the paper.

findings.claim: On least squares the curvature is constant and the gap is about a factor $4$ on the ray that attracts generic runs \cite{shulgin2026quadratic}; a large gap needs a global constant far below the curvature met, as for logistic and softmax losses (not measured for the polar step).
findings.problem: (a) Attribution : Shulgin et al. donnent le taux (1-2w)^2 sur la famille a deux amas du cas commutant (Corollaire 5 ; w = lambda_min/tr(H) pour la famille de l'annexe E.2), d'ou le facteur 4 sur ce rayon ; ils ne disent nulle part que les trajectoires generiques y sont attirees. C'est une observation numerique de l'etude, que ses propres notes classent [N], 'not proved', et posent en question ouverte, les rayons etant lineairement instables pour l'iteration commutante. Jawanpuria et al. ecrivent meme que le taux asymptotique 'varies with the initialization'. (b) Portee : le facteur 4 ne vaut que dans la queue. Sur moindres carres, a courbure constante, l'exposant moyen jusqu'a F/F_0 = 1e-6 est 8 a 13 fois le certifie, 55 a 420 fois jusqu'a 1e-2, 107 a 1750 fois au premier pas : 'a large gap needs a global constant far below the curvature met' est contredit par ce cas, que la source citee documente (p(X) = 1 pour une erreur isotrope en lignes, convergence en un pas ; le pas regle 'keeps p(X_k) near 0.6'). muPL/muop depend de la forme de l'erreur, pas de la seule courbure.
findings.evidence: arXiv:2610.30280v1 : Corollaire 5 ('p(X_k) = 4w(1-w), f(X_{k+1}) = (1-2w)^2 f(X_k)', hypotheses du Corollaire 4 = cas commutant) ; apres le Theoreme 3 : 'Row-isotropic iterates give p(X) = 1' ; 'the tuned rate alpha ~ 1.7 ... keeps p(X_k) near 0.6, whereas under line search p(X_k) decays to 0.01 within 150 iterations'. arXiv:2610.27747v1, annexe C : 'we do not know its rate in closed form. In experiments on random problems (not reported here), the measured asymptotic factor is typically smaller than the slowest invariant rate ..., and it varies with the initialization.' archive/muon/notes_spectral_theory.tex l. 800-801 ('Which of these rates a run follows is a numerical matter [N], because the rays are unstable'), l. 829 ('here it is not proved'), l. 1210-1214 ('Is the flattest ray attracting for the non-commuting iteration, and why?'). paper/audit/checks/cite-muon_ray_factor4.py (20x20, 40x20, 100x100 ; spectres k^-1, k^-2 ; departs gaussiens ; L = Lop) : exposant de queue / certifie = 4.02 a 4.23 ; exposant moyen / certifie jusqu'a 1e-2, 1e-4, 1e-6, 1e-8 : 55-420, 13-60, 8-13, 7-9 ; premier pas : 107 a 1750.
findings.proposed_fix: On least squares the curvature is constant and the gap depends on the shape of the error: $\muPL=\Lop$ for a row-isotropic error, and the gap is about a factor $4$ on the invariant ray of the flattest direction \cite[Theorem~3, Corollary~5]{shulgin2026quadratic}, which the tails of generic runs approach in our simulations (the mean exponent down to $10^{-6}$ is about $10$ times the certified one); for logistic and softmax losses the global constant is in addition far below the curvature met (not measured for the polar step).

findings.claim: With a constant spectral length $\eta$, $\max(F(W_t),F(W_{t+1}))-F_\ast\ge\muop\eta^2/8$ whenever the step is nonzero \cite[Lemma~4]{jawanpuria2026constant}
findings.problem: Le Lemme 4 n'enonce pas cette inegalite. Il donne, pour la quadratique f = 1/2 tr(X^T H X) et le facteur polaire exact (ou ns sans eps), max{||E_t||_F, ||E_{t+1}||_F} >= alpha gamma/2 (gamma = 1) et l'absence de limite pour presque tout X_0 : un plancher en distance de Frobenius, sur quadratiques, a gradient exact. Le plancher en valeur de fonction muop eta^2/8, pour F quelconque et un estimateur quelconque, est un corollaire du papier (inegalite triangulaire en norme spectrale, puis F - F_* >= (muop/2)||W - W_*||_op^2). Le calcul est exact ; le renvoi presente comme cite un enonce qui ne figure pas dans la source.
findings.evidence: arXiv:2610.27747v1, Lemme 4 : 'Let Phi be the polar map or the normalized NS iteration with eps = 0. Then for every H > 0, alpha > 0, and X_0, the iteration (2) satisfies max{||E_t||_F, ||E_{t+1}||_F} >= alpha gamma/2 whenever G_t != 0, where gamma = 1 for the polar map ..., and the iterates have no limit for almost every X_0.' Annexe D, Proposition 10, Step 1 : inegalite triangulaire. Aucune occurrence de '/8' ni de plancher en f dans le texte.
findings.proposed_fix: whenever the step is nonzero (two consecutive iterates are $\eta$ apart in spectral norm; the argument of \cite[Lemma~4]{jawanpuria2026constant})
